title: Extracellular vesicle separation from milk and infant milk formula
author: Mukhopadhya, Santoro, et al.
materials: SW Type 32 Ti swinging bucket rotor

steps.title: Prepare untreated milk whey
steps.instruction: Reconstitute infant milk formula (IMF) by mixing 4.4 g IMF powder with 30 mL freshly boiled water that has been allowed to cool to warm (not boiling) temperature; use sterile tubes and filtered deionised water for all steps. For each sample, place 50 mL of skim milk (SM) or reconstituted IMF into a centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 2,000 g for 20 min at 4 °C. If the starting milk is not defatted, first centrifuge at 6,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard the pellet, then repeat the 2,000 g 20 min 4 °C spin on the supernatant. Carefully collect the supernatant and discard any pellet. Filter the supernatant through a Whatman™ Grade 1 filter paper (150 mm diameter) placed in a glass funnel that has been folded in half and then again to form a 90° angle; pour the supernatant onto the folded paper and collect the filtrate in a fresh tube. Designate the filtrate from SM as SM_NT and from IMF as IMF_NT.

steps.title: Acetic acid treatment and filtration
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of 50 mL of SM or IMF whey to 4.6 by adding 6 N acetic acid drop‑by‑drop while stirring continuously; monitor pH with a standard pH meter (Mettler‑Toledo). Perform this step under a fume hood. After reaching pH 4.6, let the sample stand for 10 min at room temperature (20 °C–22 °C). Centrifuge the sample at 5,000 g for 30 min at 4 °C using a Sorvall ST 8 R benchtop centrifuge. Subject the resulting supernatant to a three‑step filtration: (1) filter through Whatman™ Grade 1 filter paper (150 mm) as described above, (2) pass the filtrate through a 0.45 µm syringe filter, and (3) pass the filtrate through a 0.22 µm syringe filter. Transfer 20 mL of the final filtrate to a Falcon tube. Designate the filtrate from SM as SM_AA and from IMF as IMF_AA. Store the whey at 4 °C; do not freeze.

steps.title: Isoelectric precipitation and filtration
steps.instruction: Dilute each SM or IMF sample with an equal volume of distilled water. Adjust the pH of the diluted mixture to 4.6 by adding 6 N HCl drop‑by‑drop while stirring and monitoring with a pH meter (same procedure as step 4). Perform this step under a fume hood. Place the pH‑adjusted milk on ice for 10 min, then centrifuge at 5,000 g for 30 min at 4 °C. Filter the resulting whey using the same three‑step filtration sequence described in step 6 (Whatman™ Grade 1 filter paper, followed by 0.45 µm syringe filter, then 0.22 µm syringe filter). Transfer the final filtrate to a Falcon tube and designate it as SM_IP for skim milk or IMF_IP for infant formula. Store the whey at 4 °C; do not freeze.
